title: One tag in your journal can expose your worst habit

channel.name: Andrew Builds (TradeNotes)
channel.appBlurb: a trading journal and performance analytics app

body.hook: One tag in your journal can expose your worst habit.
body.promise: Watch these sample trades. The pattern is not in the wins or the losses.

beats.narration: At first, it looks random. Wins, losses, nothing stands out. So where is it hiding?
Add one tag to every trade. Was it taken right after a loss? Yes or no. Then split.
In this sample, the trades taken right after a loss do most of the damage. Same setup. But that is not the twist.

scene.title: Split by tag
scene.note: 10 SAMPLE trades, not real results. Illustration only.

beats.narration: Here is the twist. The tag never says why. It shows which trades to reread in your own journal.

scene.sub: A question for your own data.

beats.narration: I built TradeNotes, my own trading journal, so I'm biased. It lets you tag trades and split results by tag.
So the habit was never in the results. It was in what came right before the trade. And every trade still carries risk of loss.

body.cta: Pick one tag, and log it on your next twenty trades. Not financial advice.

post.ytTitle: One journal tag that can expose your worst trading habit
post.ytDesc: Ten SAMPLE trades (not real trades) look random until you add one tag: was the trade taken right after a loss? This short shows how a tag turns a P&L into a question about your own behavior. A tag does not explain why, it shows where to look, and a handful of trades proves nothing, so check it in your own journal. Trading carries risk of loss. I built TradeNotes, so I'm biased. Part 4 of 5. Educational content only, not financial advice.
